head: DT-277
sites: `ColdSimulationProtocol.validateEnvelope` 322 (`pageCount > 9`) and 335 (`sources.length > 9`); `EconomyContext.forGroup` 1774 `slice(0, 9)` against the worker's 10-18 contexts (`PartyGoalCalculation.calculate`); owner of the number `ClanRaidExpedition.capacity`; `ColdSimulationCoordinator.requestPartyGoals` 989/1001 (timeout and refused send uncounted)
what: a clan raid expedition of more than nine (core + helpers) never forms: three bounds still say nine, in this order: a roster over 256 KB is paged one member a page and refused at 9 pages (`party_goal_send_failed`, 18 real states = 407 KB), else the group purse takes nine members while the worker built 10-18 contexts (`party_member_context_mismatch`), else the answer's sources are refused at 9 (fault, 5 s timeout holding 1 of 2 goal slots); the members stay in `party_wait` with raid shots bought and every assembly repeats; proven end to end through the real coordinator and worker for 10 and 18 members; how often a clan raid takes helpers is unknown (no save has a clan able to raid)
fix: the expedition's size named in its owner and read by the protocol; one purse function for main and worker (the leader's nine); the timeout and the refused send counted through FailureLog
why: the architecture pass's chain was wrong at its first link (only the result validator named); corrected by the planner's reproduction, scratchpad dt277-plan.md

head: DT-273
origin: player report 11-11 (server preview.22 = 6f4354a2e, bot Sawyer at 45868,34914,-3632); geodata repro 11-11
sites: `GeodataEngine.hasLineOfSight` 475-481 and `findPathSteps` 614-625 (a step needs the exit flag of the cell AND the opposite flag of the next cell); `HuntingState.tick` no-target branch 1280-1330 (wander needs a line of sight at the bot's own Z); `BotHuntingVisibility.select`
what: a hot hunter standing on a one-way geodata cell (exit flags downhill only: 7% of the cells 4000 around the report's point) has no walkable neighbour: every route fails and every mob and wander point is out of sight → it stands forever with full HP, scan pending/out_of_sight, uncounted, no situation raised; how the body got onto the cell is NOT known (a mover that steps without the pathfinder's rule: investigation)
fix: investigation first: which mover put the body there (trace), and the C4 rule for NSWE (L2J reads the leaving cell's flag only: a one-way drop is passable downhill); then one of: the engine's step rule, the mover, or a counted stuck-body situation

head: DT-274
sites: `NpcRewards.spawnGroundDrop` 27-31 (drop point: a random point 50 around the corpse, height only); `Automation.schedulePickup` 581-622 (straight run, no geodata call); copies of 'may a body go straight from A to B': `GeodataEngine.hasLineOfSight`, `Automation` 10-17 and 241-246, `MoveTo` 260-264 and 451-477, `EffectRestrictions` 207-240, `PartyCombatLootPolicy` 67-68, `HuntingState` 1328, `NpcWander` 198
what: a drop can land on a static object's footprint (a tree's raised ring) and the pickup runs a straight line to it with a linearly interpolated Z: the body ends on a cell it cannot leave (reproduced on the exact point of DT-273: 45868,34914,-3510 from open ground 76 away); 0.22-0.27% of drops in that field (about 1 in 400) strand their picker, who then stands forever (DT-273), uncounted; a player's drop there is out of reach too
fix: one engine answer for 'how far does a straight move from A toward B go' (C4 moveCheck): the drop lands where a walk from the corpse reaches, the pickup stops where the step rule stops; count the hunter with no usable route (FailureLog)

head: AI-16
what: a melee bot's pickup starts at the hit point (drop spawn), mid-swing; the swing-end timer finds its target dead and abortAll cancels the pickup timer without the completion callback → `partyGroundPickupInProgress` stays set, the loot guard holds every tick → the bot stands 8 s beside its drop (when the drop is farther than it runs in the swing's last 36%; solo hunters and melee companions)
fix: start the pickup at swing end, as C4 (no move inside a swing): no start while the swing runs, and the swing end with a dead target starts the queued pickup instead of returning; in-progress read from Automation's pickup, not a second flag with an 8 s timeout
